lead: The experiments support explicit contributions, a generated API contract with real boundary fixtures, stable operation identities, and complete cached-scope refreshes. They also found concrete gaps in the original schema and restore proposals.

choices.title: Explicit contributor rows
choices.text: Keep manual, source and unknown legacy adjustments separate. Source corrections replace one contribution. Full command history was not needed for the exercised behaviors.

choices.title: Generated types plus validators
choices.text: Rust/utoipa with openapi-typescript and Ajv standalone is the stronger of the two exercised pipelines. Enum closure, suppression, dates and numeric range still need explicit contract decisions.

choices.title: Stable operation IDs
choices.text: Deduplicate by client installation and immutable operation ID. Server generation belongs in cache and conditional-edit versions. A restored snapshot still needs explicit source reconciliation.

choices.title: Complete scope refreshes
choices.text: Replace cached date ranges and preserve the separate outbox. Use scoped, generation-aware and time-aware validators. The traces do not establish a need for an initial change feed.

product_choices: Define manual contribution set separately from aggregate replacement or a pinned override. Decide activity-day attribution and who may make restored source history authoritative. Passing traces cannot choose those meanings.
next: Specify contributor rows and a small versioned API, then build one manual observation, one versioned source-day replacement and one chart-independent series query through the real Rust HTTP adapter and generated client. Prove migration and device behavior before replacing current consumers.
limits: Synthetic observations, not production acceptance. Storage variants share a semantic reducer. SQLite rollback/restore and cache-only loopback HTTP were exercised; production adapters, concurrent writers, process kills, real-data migration and React Native/Hermes were not. No performance benefit was measured.
review: Independent review pending. The source runners, observations and decision trail will be audited before final delivery.
api_summary: Both generated paths accepted the exercised Rust-serialized outputs, but neither exactly matched raw Rust input parsing. The prototype exposed disagreements that schema generation alone would not catch.
api_lessons: Full-i64 JSON numbers lost digits in JavaScript. Safe-range numbers worked for the exercised ordinary values. Decide the supported product range before narrowing any legacy contract; opaque version tokens avoid arithmetic encoding.

Canonical decimal strings preserved full-i64 values, but generated regex validation did not enforce i64 arithmetic bounds. The matching BigInt refinement is handwritten and remains a second authority.

Unknown enum fields and suppressed goals behaved differently across Rust, emitted schema and decoders. Ajv followed the emitted schema more closely; it cannot repair a schema that does not describe Rust's behavior.
The comparison Zod generator is deprecated and its exported scalar roots lost constraints. This supports a toolchain candidate, not a claim that every Zod-based generator fails.
Dates, duplicate JSON keys, lexical integers and interval ordering need explicit boundary/domain rules. Generated types compile; that alone does not prove parser or product equivalence.
